clue.text: Intimidate labourer, who looks after cattle

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who looks after cattle'

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Someone bullies a farm worker employed to tend the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowhand is a ranch or farm worker employed to tend livestock.

clue.text: Tart made with shellfish found lying on ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, lying on means placed above, so the first item goes on top of the second

parts.note: a crab is a shellfish
a bed is a piece of ground, as in a flower bed or sea bed

explanation.surface: A seafood pastry is made with shellfish found on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tart looks like a pastry dish, but it is the adjective meaning sharp-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabbed means sour or cross in temper, the same sharpness as a tart reply.

clue.text: Sea mammal must suffer, concealing nothing that's very hairy

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that is very hairy'

parts.note: the walrus is a tusked sea mammal

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the word holds the empty symbol within it

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: A sea mammal has to suffer for having such a shaggy face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' is the letter O, a crossword convention from its zero-like shape; 'suffer' is a verb here, not the surface's sense of enduring the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick bushy one drooping over the mouth, very hairy indeed.

clue.text: Wicked lady suppressing poetry in a hostile way

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted and corrupted, so the letters are scrambled
suppressing means holding something down within, so one part is kept inside the other

parts.note: the letters of lady rearranged
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A wicked woman censors poems in an unfriendly manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversely means unfavourably or in opposition, a synonym of with hostility.

clue.text: Lift up the violin, which is played in the pub

definitions.text: which is played in the pub
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'the game which is played in the pub'

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up sends the letters from bottom to top, so they read backwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: Someone raises a fiddle to play a tune in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Strad, short for Stradivarius, the famous make of violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is the classic British pub game of throwing small arrows at a board.

clue.text: Ines squeezes Henry and draws breath

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to grip it tightly between both sides, so one name wraps round the other

parts.note: taken as written
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Ines hugs Henry so tightly she has to gasp for air.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is not H here but the nickname Hal, which sits inside IN-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhale is to take air into the lungs, the same as breathing in.

clue.text: Thin Biro I misused as a preventative

indicators.note: something misused is handled wrongly, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone puts a slim ballpoint pen to an odd use, as a blocker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Biro is a ballpoint pen in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhibitor is a substance or thing that slows or blocks a process, so it prevents it.

clue.text: Expects a piece of chop, escalope etc

indicators.note: a piece of means only a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding, completing the menu picture

explanation.surface: A diner anticipates a cut of meat from the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope for something is to anticipate it, close to expecting it.

clue.text: Newspaper editorials are superior pieces

parts.note: leading means foremost or superior
articles are pieces, items or written pieces

explanation.surface: The editor boasts that the opinion columns are the best writing in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading articles, or leaders, are the editorial opinion pieces in a British newspaper.

clue.text: New eyes cast on the flying squad

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about or moulded anew, so these letters take a fresh shape

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh eyes are cast over a crack police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Squad is a London police unit; rhyming slang (Sweeney Todd for Flying Squad) gives its nickname, also a 1970s TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sweeney is Cockney rhyming slang for the Metropolitan Police's Flying Squad.

clue.text: Everywhere a Latin sweetheart is on the spot

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin
a sweetheart is a lover
the spot and the place both mean the location in question; 'on' just places it after

explanation.surface: A Latin lover seems to turn up wherever you look, always right there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered in every direction, so it is a looser way of saying everywhere.

clue.text: More pornographic smear grips one finally

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it inside, so the smear word encloses the letter

parts.note: to blur is to smudge or smear

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of one

explanation.surface: A tabloid smear story gets more and more salacious as it takes hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is a slang word for sexually explicit or smutty, so the comparative means more indecent.

clue.text: Christian martyr looks silly in a bassinet

indicators.note: something that looks silly is in a ridiculous state, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown saint lying in a baby's crib would look absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: A bassinet is a hooded basket cradle for a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Sebastian was an early Christian killed for his faith, famously shot with arrows.

clue.text: Try yours to solve the lost set wandering?

definitions.note: stands for 'your damnedest' in the phrase 'try your damnedest'

indicators.note: wandering things stray from their place, so these letters move out of order

parts.note: the lost souls are the damned
the letters of set rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver is urged to do their best with a tricky anagram of a lost set.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the phrase 'try your damnedest': 'yours' stands in for the answer, making the definition a cryptic hint rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Your damnedest is your utmost effort, as in the idiom 'do your damnedest'.

clue.text: Spellbound wench can't get going before start of day

indicators.note: not able to get going means the word cannot start, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before it loses its first letter
ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: start of points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of day

explanation.surface: A bewitched serving girl is unable to start work before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in can't hides the split: 'wench can't get going' is wench headless, not the word can.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanted means under a spell, bewitched, so spellbound.

clue.text: Boy riding horse gets covered with mud

indicators.note: a rider sits astride a mount, legs either side, so the boy's letters straddle the horse

parts.note: taken as written
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A lad goes riding and comes home caked in mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy describes ground that is wet and muddy like a bog; here stretched to mean mud-covered.

clue.text: Yeoman of the Guard is not a vegetarian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the popular name for a Tower of London warder
second meaning, read literally: someone who eats meat from cattle

explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen Warders of the Tower of London, often confused with the Yeomen of the Guard, are nicknamed for their historic meat ration.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belongs to the ceremonial royal bodyguard, and literally names a person who eats cow meat.

clue.text: Speak about copper turning rude

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speaking word goes around the metal

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: turning round sets the metal symbol back to front

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman, spoken to, turns rude in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but here it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy means cheeky or impertinent, a mild sense of rude.

clue.text: Prepares children to go beneath the ocean

indicators.note: in a down clue, going beneath means placed lower, so these come after

parts.note: an ocean is a sea
sons are children

explanation.surface: Someone readies their kids for a dive under the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To season is to prepare, as timber or a cook's dish is prepared for use.

clue.text: You could meet me on the stairs!

definitions.text: You could meet me on the stairs!

parts.words: You could meet me on the stairs!
parts.note: surface reading: a person on the staircase you might bump into

parts.words: You could meet me on the stairs!
parts.note: setter's reading: a fitting fixed at each step to hold the floor covering in place

explanation.walkthrough: The 'me' sounds like a person, but it is a household fixture that lives on every stair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stair rods are metal bars fixed across the back of each step to hold a runner of floor covering down.

clue.text: Treats — some girls still prefer them to jeans!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tends a wound, as a nurse does

definitions.text: some girls still prefer them to jeans
definitions.note: plural noun phrase defined by the description

explanation.walkthrough: Treats looks like a noun for sweets but is the verb for caring for a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to treat it, and frocks are the garment worn instead of denim.

clue.text: Dafter losing head — drawback later

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, before it loses its first letter

indicators.note: back means the word is read from end to start

parts.note: the word draw, with back as its turnaround signal, then read backwards

explanation.surface: A sillier person beheaded is a later drawback, a joke with no clear scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like one word meaning a disadvantage, but it splits into draw and an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterward is an adverb meaning at a subsequent time, a straight synonym.

clue.text: He's found steeped in rum, so gets a discharge

indicators.note: steeped in means soaked and immersed, so one part is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the 's being 'is'

explanation.surface: A man soaked in rum ends up with a runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucus discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Excitement when a mother needs the doctor

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: There's commotion when a mum has to call out the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is exciting or emotional events, a synonym for excitement as in 'a day full of drama'.

clue.text: Best hat turned towards the east

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The finest hat is the one turned to face the rising sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile as slang for a hat is old-fashioned but common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, the select few at the top.

clue.text: The band stops dead for seated spectators

definitions.note: the seats stand for the people sitting in them

parts.note: an orchestra is a band of musicians
an engine that stalls stops dead

explanation.surface: The musicians suddenly halt to let the audience take their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British theatre the stalls are the seats on the ground floor nearest the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra stalls are the front rows of theatre seating, so by extension the audience seated there.

clue.text: Horse coming round in the morning proceeded quickly

indicators.note: coming round means going around something, so the horse word wraps the time of day

parts.note: a steed is a horse
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A horse rounds the bend at dawn and sets off at a gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam ahead is to move fast, as a steam train or ship does.

clue.text: A queen sleeps, then stops

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for regina, Latin for queen
to rest is to sleep or relax

explanation.surface: A monarch naps and then comes to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrests is a verb meaning halts or checks, as in arresting a decline.
